Honey Galette

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 45 min

The Feast of the Ass, a medieval festival celebrated in parts of Europe, was known for its joyous and often irreverent spirit, marking a break from solemnity. While specific culinary traditions for this unique holiday are scarce, a rustic Honey Galette, with its simple elegance and natural sweetness, would have been a welcome treat at any festive gathering. This free-form pastry, highlighting the golden richness of honey, offers a taste of old-world charm perfect for a historical celebration.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/4 cups (150 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, very cold and cut into small cubes
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) ice water, plus more if needed
  • 2 medium apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Granny Smith), peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) honey, plus 1 tablespoon for brushing
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon cornstarch or all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • Pinch of ground nutmeg
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • 1 tablespoon turbinado sugar (for sprinkling)

Method

  1. To make the dough, combine flour and salt in a large bowl or food processor. Add the cold butter cubes and cut in with a pastry blender or pulse until the mixture resembles coarse meal with pea-sized butter pieces.
  2. Gradually add the ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form the dough into a flat disk, wrap tightly in plastic, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
  3. While the dough chills, prepare the filling. In a large bowl, combine the thinly sliced apples, 1/4 cup (60 ml) honey, lemon juice, cornstarch, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Toss gently to coat all the apple slices evenly.
  4. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  5. On a lightly floured surface, roll the chilled dough into a rough 12-inch (30 cm) circle. Don't worry if it's not perfectly round; the rustic look is part of a galette's charm.
  6. Carefully transfer the rolled dough to the prepared baking sheet.
  7. Arrange the apple mixture in the center of the dough, leaving a 2-inch (5 cm) border around the edges. Dot the top of the apple mixture with the 2 tablespoons of small butter pieces.
  8. Carefully fold the dough border up and over the edges of the filling, pleating it as you go, leaving the center of the apples exposed.
  9. In a small bowl, whisk the large egg to create an egg wash. Brush the folded crust generously with the beaten egg and then sprinkle it with turbinado sugar.
  10. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the apples are tender and bubbling.
  11. Remove the galette from the oven. While it is still warm, brush the exposed apple filling with the remaining 1 tablespoon of honey to give it a beautiful glaze.
  12. Let the galette cool on the baking sheet for at least 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche, a scoop of vanilla ice cream, or a drizzle of extra honey.
  • For a nutty flavor and added texture, incorporate 1/4 cup (25 g) chopped walnuts or pecans into the apple filling.
  • Feel free to experiment with other firm fruits like pears or peaches in place of apples, adjusting spices as desired.
